_about: Full artist cards. Keys must match the real name used on the board (the part after '=>' in chart.json, or the name itself). The data pipeline will fill this in for every artist.

Chuck Berry.whyTheyMatter: Wrote the rulebook for rock guitar: the double-stop intro, the duckwalk, and lyrics about cars, school, and teenagers. If rock had a founding father, the paternity test comes back here.

seenIn.title: Back to the Future
seenIn.note: “Johnny B. Goode,” played by Marty at the school dance

seenIn.title: Pulp Fiction
seenIn.note: “You Never Can Tell,” the Jack Rabbit Slim's twist contest

Little Richard.whyTheyMatter: Pounded piano, a pompadour, and a scream that made everyone else sound polite. He brought gospel's intensity and pure showmanship to rock and roll.

Elvis Presley.whyTheyMatter: The Memphis truck driver who fused country and R&B at Sun Studio and carried it into every living room in America. The first true rock star.

seenIn.title: Lilo & Stitch
seenIn.note: “Hound Dog,” “Suspicious Minds,” and more; Lilo's favorite

seenIn.title: Elvis
seenIn.note: Baz Luhrmann's biopic, built on his catalog

Buddy Holly.whyTheyMatter: Glasses, a Stratocaster, and songs he wrote himself for a self-contained band. Two guitars, bass, and drums became the standard lineup because of him.

The Beatles.whyTheyMatter: Started as a Chuck Berry and Little Richard cover band in Hamburg clubs, then rewrote what a pop song and an album could be, about every six months.

seenIn.title: A Hard Day's Night
seenIn.note: Their own movie, and a blueprint for music videos

seenIn.title: Across the Universe
seenIn.note: A musical built entirely from their songs

seenIn.title: Yesterday
seenIn.note: A world where only one man remembers them

Rolling Stones.whyTheyMatter: Named themselves after a Muddy Waters song and stayed the bluesiest band of the invasion. Sixty-plus years later, still touring.

seenIn.title: Full Metal Jacket
seenIn.note: “Paint It Black” over the end credits

Cream.whyTheyMatter: Eric Clapton, Jack Bruce, and Ginger Baker: the first supergroup. They took blues standards, stretched them into long improvised jams, and cranked the volume, laying track for hard rock.

seenIn.title: Goodfellas
seenIn.note: “Sunshine of Your Love” in the bar scene

Led Zeppelin.whyTheyMatter: Took Cream's blues-rock blueprint and made it enormous: Page's riffs, Plant's wail, and Bonham's drums. Hard rock's heavyweight champions.

seenIn.title: School of Rock
seenIn.note: “Immigrant Song” (Jack Black filmed a video begging the band for permission)

seenIn.title: Thor: Ragnarok
seenIn.note: “Immigrant Song” in both big battle scenes
